newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia to introduce new blue-chip index Jan 97.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia to introduce new blue-chip index Jan 97.

text.p: Slovenia will introduce a new blue-chip share index in January of next year, replacing the existing SBI index, stock exchange president Drasko Veselinovic said on Wednesday.
"In the new year we will adopt a completely new index that will be weighted to represent market capitalisation and will include new companies," Veselinovic told Reuters in an interview.

He said the new index would include about 10 shares and would be comparable with indexes on other international stock exchanges. Shares would have to fulfil criteria on liquidity and market capitalisation, Veselinovic added. Details will be announced in December.

The current SBI index of seven shares will continue trading until the end of the year. It was first introduced in June 1994 but has recently come under fire from traders because sharp movements in individual shares can throw the whole market out of kilter.
"We are aware of the shortcomings of this index but we couldn't have done any better than we did at the time," Veselinovic said.
Tomaz Rotar, bourse deputy chief executive, said the stock exchange would probably expand the existing SBI index within two weeks to include some newly privatised companies.
Pharmaceutical company Lek and food company Droga were among the most likely candidates, he added.
